title: Supervisory Risks in Crypto-Assets and Digital Finance
summary: A structured framework for identifying and assessing risks across digital finance, showing how market, operational, cyber and governance risks interact within firms and markets.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: A structured framework for identifying and assessing risks across digital finance, showing how market, operational, cyber and governance risks interact within firms and markets.
Learning Objectives: Identify the key risk categories in digital finance
Analyse operational, cyber and governance risks in crypto firms
Evaluate market volatility and market abuse risks
Syllabus: Market volatility, leverage and price dynamics
Operational failures, cyber threats and attack vectors
Governance and control failures: lessons from firm collapses
Market abuse and manipulation in crypto markets
Intended Audience: Supervisors and authorisation staff responsible for, or moving into, oversight of virtual asset service providers
Risk, policy, legal and financial crime specialists working on digital finance
Senior managers shaping the authority's approach to crypto-assets and digital finance
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision, authorisation or financial crime work is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)
